A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DR-COSARC study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A1–A5 are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation experiments across ten settings and analyses of seven real datasets, including detailed appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds experiments on the double-robustness adjustment and imputation stability.

M1.justification: The imputation and fixed/adaptive conformal calibration procedures remain the same. The final minimum-with-uncalibrated-quantile adjustment made explicit in v2 Algorithm 2 already appears in v1 Algorithm A4; this resolves inconsistent documentation rather than introducing a component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same ten synthetic distributions and seven real datasets listed in Tables A1–A3. The new diagnostic experiments reuse synthetic settings 1–3.

E2.justification: v2 Figure A9 adds the comparison variants 'DR-COSARC (fixed, not DR)' and 'DR-COSARC (adaptive, not DR)', which omit the final adjustment. The existing Oracle, Uncalibrated, Naive CQR, and KM Decensoring comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The new stability experiment in Appendix A3.7 holds datasets and fitted models fixed across imputations, uses 100 test points instead of the usual 1000, and measures the coefficient of variation across calibration-set sizes. Existing benchmark protocols, including the real-data 60/20/20 split, remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A3.6–A3.7 add two substantive diagnostic questions: how removing the double-robustness adjustment affects predictions, and how stochastic imputation affects algorithmic stability. Earlier sample-size, covariate-count, and model sensitivity analyses remain; v2 main Figure 2 relocates v1 Figure A2 rather than adding another experiment.

E5.justification: The new stability study reports 10 independent imputation seeds per fixed dataset, averaging over 20 independent data realizations, with error bars representing two standard errors. The existing experiments' 100 repetitions and real-data uncertainty reporting are retained.

E6.justification: Figure A9 adds coverage and lower-bound results for variants without the adjustment. Figure A10 newly reports greater imputation variability for the fixed-cutoff method than for adaptive DR-COSARC and KM Decensoring. Existing benchmark findings and numerical entries in Tables A4–A7 are unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation (4) corrects the imputation normalizer from an integral over zero to the observed time to an integral from the observed time to infinity, matching the truncated density and the existing Appendix A5.1 proof. Assumption 3.2(ii) also corrects a malformed equality; the principal theorems and proofs are retained.

C1.justification: Both versions claim an extension from type-I to right-censored survival inference, asymptotic double robustness, and improved reliability in challenging modeling settings. Abstract revisions and additional supporting experiments do not materially change these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that the finite-sample bounds are too loose for practical use and identifies algorithmic variability from splitting and imputation as a limitation. It adds possible remedies using e-values or full conformal inference and explains the rationale for sharing fitted survival models across comparators.

D1.justification: The Software Availability statement retains the implementation repository but drops v1's explicit promise of code reproducing all results. This narrows the documented reproducibility information without establishing that any code was removed. Existing implementation and preprocessing details are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds Vovk and Wang (2021) and Bashari et al. (2023) to support future work on reducing randomness, and removes the separately listed Zaffran et al. (2024) reference. Positioning against the principal survival-inference methods remains unchanged; publication updates for retained references are bibliographic edits.

P1.justification: v2 substantially reorganizes the experimental narrative: the censoring-model-quality study moves into main Section 4.3, the experiment roadmap expands, and Appendix A3 replaces its mixed discussion/figure grouping with topic-specific subsections. Introduction and method prose are revised, the redundant short technical review is removed, and algorithm references are corrected.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figures A9–A10, moves v1 Figure A2 into the main text as Figure 2 with a revised legend layout, and regroups appendix plots. Author affiliations and several display details change, while existing tables and most graphical designs remain intact.

improvement.justification: v2 improves consistency by correcting Equation (4) and aligning main Algorithm 2 with the existing appendix specification. The new ablation and controlled stability study strengthen targeted empirical support and expose a practical limitation. These are bounded gains over v1's already extensive evidence; the less explicit reproduction-code statement is a small documentation drawback.
